newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq said fired missiles against U.S. warplanes.
newsitem.headline: Iraq said fired missiles against U.S. warplanes.

text.p: Iraq said on Saturday that its air defence units fired surface-to-air missiles against the United States and allied warplanes policing the no-fly zones in southern and northern Iraq.

"Our brave air defence men have confronted the hostile warplanes and fired surface-to-air missiles but they missed their targets this time," Iraqi state-run television said quoting a military spokesman.

"We will continue to resist it (U.S. and allied warplanes' violation of Iraq's space) departing from the legitimate right to defend ourselves and sovereignty," the spokesman said. The statement did not say when the incident took place.

"We stress our firm stand that the continuation of American warplanes' violation of our air space is a continuation of threats by the U.S. and those taking part with it to our sovereignty and national security," the spokesman said.

The United States said it could not confirm that Iraq had fired surface-to-air missiles against U.S. warplanes policing the no-fly zones, which were set up after the 1991 Gulf War that ousted Iraqi troops from Kuwait.
"At this time we have no information to confirm that," said a White House spokesman, Barry Toiv in Washington. He said U.S. officials were checking out the report.
The Iraqi foreign ministry in a statement said Baghdad would ignore warning by the United States and Britain not to boost or mobilise air defence units south of the 33rd parallel.

The United States extended the southern no-fly zone by one degree, almost to the outskirts of Baghdad, after Iraqi troops intervened in northern Iraq last weekend to help a Kurdish group wrest a key city from a rival Kurdish group.

The statement carried by state television said the two countries had sent a message to Iraq warning against attempts to repair air defence units hit by U.S. missiles on Tuesday and Wednesday in retaliation for Iraq's military intervention.
It said Washington and London warned Iraq against shifting the positions of its anit-aircraft missiles within the southern air-exclusion zone.
"The cursed parallels which the colonial Americans and British are trying to impose are finished and non-existent," the statement said.
It said: "We shall hit with all force the violation of our air space by British and Americans planes."
The statement said Iraq air defence units throughout the country would hit "any hostile air target which violates Iraq's air space."
The statement said the United States and Britain faxed their message to Iraq's U.N. mission in New York when Iraq's envoy there refused to receive ambassadors from the two countries.
Earlier in the day, Iraqis were urged to declare holy war on the United States.

"We have no alternative...but to declare jihad (holy war) and fight them (Americans) until the last drop in Iraqis' vain...and strongly reject all their means and commandments," said Babel, the newspaper of President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday.
